text.p: Following is factfile on Steve
Coppell who resigned on Friday as manager of Manchester City
after 33 days because of "huge pressure."
1955: Born in Liverpool.
1974: Signed as part-timer for Tranmere. Went on to score 10
goals in 38 league appearances.
1975: Joined Manchester United for aroound $100,000.
1976: Won England under-23 cap against Hungary. Gained
economics degree from Liverpool University.
1977: Won F.A. Cup winners' medal as United beat Liverpool
2-1 in final. Won first England cap.
1981: Sustained knee injury in international against Hungary
which was to eventually end his career.
1983: Won last of 42 England caps. Retired.
1984: Made unsuccessful bid to resurrect career by
undergoing three months of intensive treatment in an Amsterdam
clinic. Became then-youngest manager in the league when he took
charge of Crystal Palace.
1989: Took Palace to promotion to old first division.
Suffered low point of managerial career when Palace slumped 9-0
at Liverpool.
1990: Guided Palace to Wembley for the first time in their
history with F.A. Cup final date against his old club,
Manchester United. A thrilling match ended 3-3 after extra time
but Palace lost the replay 1-0.
1993: Quit in close-season after Palace relegated from
premier league.
1995: Returned to Crystal Palace as director of football.
1996: Became manager at Manchester City but forced out by
ill health after just 33 days.
